name: Vaishata
title: Persian Queen Who Was Deposed
summary: Vaishata (also known as Vashti) was the queen of Persia and wife to King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I). She is known for refusing to obey the king's command to appear before his guests at a great banquet, which led to her being deposed as queen. Her removal paved the way for Esther to become the new queen.

keyEvents.title: The King's Great Banquet
keyEvents.description: King Ahasuerus held a great banquet for all his princes and servants that lasted 180 days, followed by a seven-day banquet for the people in the fortress of Susa.

keyEvents.title: Vaishata's Own Banquet
keyEvents.description: At the same time as the king's celebration, Queen Vaishata held her own banquet for the women in King Ahasuerus' royal palace.

keyEvents.title: The King's Command to Vaishata
keyEvents.description: On the seventh day of the banquet, when the king was in good spirits from wine, he commanded seven eunuchs to bring Queen Vaishata wearing the royal crown to display her beauty before the princes and the people.

keyEvents.title: Vaishata's Refusal
keyEvents.description: Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command delivered by his officials. This made the king very angry, and his fury burned within him.

keyEvents.title: Consultation with the Wise Men
keyEvents.description: The king consulted his wise men about what should be done to Queen Vashti according to the law, because she had not obeyed the king's command. Memukan proposed that she be deposed to prevent other women in the kingdom from following her example.

keyEvents.title: Vashti Deposed as Queen
keyEvents.description: The king followed Memukan's advice and sent letters to all provinces stating that Vashti should no longer come before King Ahasuerus, and that her royal position should be given to someone better than she. This later led to Esther being chosen as the new queen.
